parts.visual:
A startup builds an incredibly complex AI calendar app. The technology is genius, but the business fails. Nobody buys the app, and they run out of money. Apple steps in and 'buys' the startup for $10 Million. The day after the paperwork is signed, Apple completely shuts down the calendar app and moves the 5 engineers to work on Siri.

The Acqui-hire:
1. The Definition: An 'Acquisition-Hire'. The acquiring company does not care about the startup's product, users, or revenue. They are literally just buying the company as a legal trick to recruit the brilliant engineers.
2. The Soft Landing: For a failing startup, an acqui-hire prevents the embarrassment of bankruptcy. The VCs get a tiny fraction of their money back, the founders get high-paying jobs at a Giant, and the product is quietly buried in a graveyard.
parts.audio: In Silicon Valley, an amazing engineering team is worth more than a mediocre business. A tech giant will happily pay millions of dollars to destroy your product, just to get their hands on the brains that built it.

questions.question: Why would Google spend $10 Million on an 'Acqui-hire' instead of just putting up a job posting to hire 5 engineers?
options: Google doesn't have a job website.

Team Cohesion. Hiring 5 random, brilliant engineers who don't know each other takes months of recruiting, and they might fight. An acqui-hire buys a pre-assembled, battle-tested team that already knows how to ship code together flawlessly.
questions.correct_answer: Team Cohesion. Hiring 5 random, brilliant engineers who don't know each other takes months of recruiting, and they might fight. An acqui-hire buys a pre-assembled, battle-tested team that already knows how to ship code together flawlessly.
questions.explanation: You are buying a functional organism, not individual organs.

questions.question: Listen to the VC reacting to an acqui-hire. Why is the VC unhappy with a $5 Million acqui-hire?
questions.tts_text: The press release says it's a great exit. It's a lie. I invested $4 Million into this company. In a $5 Million acqui-hire, most of the cash goes into retention bonuses to keep the engineers from quitting. As an investor, I lost almost everything.
options: Because the VC wanted to work at Google.

The Illusion of Success. Acqui-hires are often PR cover-ups for a failed startup. The structure of the deal ensures the engineers get highly paid jobs (Golden Handcuffs), but the investors usually take a massive financial loss.
Because the product is too good.
questions.correct_answer: The Illusion of Success. Acqui-hires are often PR cover-ups for a failed startup. The structure of the deal ensures the engineers get highly paid jobs (Golden Handcuffs), but the investors usually take a massive financial loss.
questions.explanation: It is an exit for the talent, not the capital.

questions.question: What happens to the startup's actual product (the app, the website) after an acqui-hire?
options: It is 'Sunsetted'. The giant company immediately emails all the users saying 'The app will shut down in 30 days'. The giant did not buy the app to maintain it; they bought the app to free up the engineers to work on the giant's own projects.
It becomes the giant's main product.
questions.correct_answer: It is 'Sunsetted'. The giant company immediately emails all the users saying 'The app will shut down in 30 days'. The giant did not buy the app to maintain it; they bought the app to free up the engineers to work on the giant's own projects.
questions.explanation: The product was just a resume for the team.

questions.question: Why do acquiring companies heavily use 'Vesting Schedules' during an acqui-hire?
options: To prevent the talent from fleeing. If Apple pays a founder $2 Million to join, the founder doesn't get the cash today. It 'vests' over 4 years. If the founder quits Apple after 6 months because they hate corporate life, they lose the money.
questions.correct_answer: To prevent the talent from fleeing. If Apple pays a founder $2 Million to join, the founder doesn't get the cash today. It 'vests' over 4 years. If the founder quits Apple after 6 months because they hate corporate life, they lose the money.
questions.explanation: You aren't just buying them; you are bribing them to stay.

pairs.match: Buying a failing startup solely to acquire its brilliant engineering team
The polite corporate term for shutting down and killing the startup's product
The high value of buying a group of people who already work perfectly together
Avoiding messy bankruptcy by letting a giant company absorb the team
